correctness.rationale: An affine join of k quadrilaterals has dimension 3k-1, 4k facets and 4k vertices. Every vertex lies on 4k-2 facets, so has excess k-1. The cited published vanishing-order lemma applies to every nonnegative rational GBC common denominator. A polynomial of degree k-1 with order at least k-1 at all affinely spanning vertices would be a nonzero top homogeneous polynomial invariant under a spanning set of translations, a contradiction. Thus the lower bound is k. Homogenizing Wachspress coordinates of each quadrilateral gives explicit polynomial numerator/denominator expressions of degrees at most k+1/k, with positivity, normalization and affine precision. All boundary values extend continuously. Exact rational checker passed 336 examples for k=2..8; finite cases are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Minimal rational barycentric denominator degree is an active geometric interpolation invariant. The exact all-shapes classification on an infinite family of high-dimensional non-simple joins closes a one-degree gap left by the published local theory; the spanning-excess principle is a reusable structural obstruction. Joining k parallelograms raises the exact degree from zero for the Cartesian product to k for the join, an unbounded natural operation-dependent separation, not a shape-specific normalization trick.
